quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: A team scenario, but the clue is in the first sound. Does the tongue tip touch?
quests.explanation: You heard "leading": the tongue tip tapped the ridge behind the upper teeth. "Reading" curls back with no contact.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ sounds clear and light; /r/ sounds darker and slightly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip: contact for /l/, hover for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: Put it in the file, please.
quests.hint: The stressed word starts with either friction or a burst.
quests.explanation: In this phrase "file" began with a hiss from the lip and teeth. "Pile" begins with a lip pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The burst of a stop is sudden and short; friction lasts as long as you keep blowing.
quests.mouthPosition: Try holding each sound: you can prolong the fricative but not the stop.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel either glides or stays wide and short.
quests.explanation: It was "plan": a short, wide vowel with no glide. "Plane" glides upward and lasts longer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ is a long gliding vowel that ends high and forward; /æ/ is a short, open vowel with no glide. Look for a vowel that moves versus one that stays wide open.
quests.mouthPosition: For /eɪ/ begin half open and let the jaw rise. For /æ/ drop the jaw and keep it low.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Where does the vowel start: half open or fully open?
quests.explanation: Here, "raise" started at half open and glided a short way. "Rise" starts wide open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ glides from a mid-front position up toward /ɪ/, while /aɪ/ starts with a wide-open mouth and glides up. The starting point differs: half-open for /eɪ/, fully open for /aɪ/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /aɪ/ open the jaw wide first, then close it. For /eɪ/ begin half open and close a short distance.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same ending. What happens at the very beginning?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "deadline": the tongue tip closed and released with a voiced burst. "Headline" begins with a breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /h/ is only breath from the throat; /d/ is a voiced stop, closed by the tongue tip against the ridge behind the upper teeth and released with a buzz.
quests.mouthPosition: For /d/ press the tongue tip on the ridge and release with voice. For /h/ keep the tongue relaxed and breathe out into the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Are the lips rounded in the strong syllable?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "worker" had loose lips and a neutral vowel. "Walker" has rounded lips and a darker vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is a long central vowel with unrounded lips; /ɔː/ is a long back vowel with clearly rounded lips. Same length, different lip shape and tongue position.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɜː/ keep the lips loose and the tongue in the centre of the mouth. For /ɔː/ round the lips into a circle and pull the tongue back.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a hiss squeezed in front of the first consonant.
quests.explanation: That was "team": no hiss, just a breathy /t/. "Steam" opens with /s/ and a softer /t/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for the initial hiss: present in the /s/-cluster, absent in the plain word.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the /s/ a moment before the stop.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: A hum or a breath at the start?
quests.explanation: This time, "meeting" started with a lip-closed hum. "Heating" starts with a puff of breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /m/ is a hum through the nose with the lips closed; /h/ is only breath from the throat with the lips open and nothing closing the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ close the lips and hum before the vowel. For /h/ leave the lips open and breathe out.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the very first sound, before the vowel gets going. Is it a hum or just breath?
quests.explanation: The word was "mouse": the lips closed for a hum. "House" starts with breath only.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /m/ is a hum through the nose with the lips closed; /h/ is only breath from the throat with the lips open and nothing closing the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ close the lips and hum before the vowel. For /h/ leave the lips open and breathe out.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end with a hiss from the lip. Compare the lips in the vowel.
quests.explanation: In this phrase "cuff" had neutral lips and a flat vowel. "Cough" rounds the lips and is deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue back and lips rounded make /ɒ/; tongue central and lips unrounded make /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ʌ/ with a relaxed jaw and no lip tension; add gentle rounding to move toward /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first syllable ends the same way. What starts it?
quests.explanation: You heard "dizzy": the tongue tip released at the ridge. "Busy" begins with the lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lips versus tongue tip: the bilabial stop closes at the lips; the alveolar stop closes at the ridge behind the upper teeth. The vowel transitions into each differ slightly.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the lips for the bilabial stop; touch the tongue tip to the ridge for the alveolar stop.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the strong vowel: half open or tight?
quests.explanation: Here, "better" opened the jaw a little more. "Bitter" is tighter and thinner.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is short and high-ish with the jaw nearly closed; /e/ is also short but the jaw opens further and the tongue lowers toward the middle.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw almost shut with relaxed lips. For /e/ lower the jaw slightly so a fingertip could fit between the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Long and open, or short and rounded?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "cast": the jaw dropped wide and the vowel stayed long. "Cost" is short and rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is short with a rounded lip shape; /ɑː/ is long with the jaw opened wide and the lips neutral. Length and lip shape both help, and /ɑː/ lasts about twice as long.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɑː/ drop the jaw fully and keep the lips flat. For /ɒ/ open less and round the lips slightly, and end the vowel sooner.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a curled /r/ after the /t/?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "tooth" went straight from /t/ to the vowel. "Truth" puts an /r/ in between.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word has an extra /r/ right after the first consonant. That /r/ makes the beginning of the word sound curled and slightly longer, and the first stop loses some of its crispness.
quests.mouthPosition: After the first consonant, curl the tongue tip back for /r/ before the vowel. Without it, the consonant moves straight into the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The endings match, so notice whether the tongue tip touches at the beginning.
quests.explanation: That was "wrist": the tongue tip curled back and did not touch. "List" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth, letting air flow around the sides; British /r/ is made with the tongue tip curled slightly back and not touching anything, often with lips a little rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /l/ press the tongue tip firmly against the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep it away from the roof of the mouth, lips slightly rounded.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a tongue-tip tap after the /f/?
quests.explanation: This time, "flight" had a tap of the tongue tip on the ridge after the /f/. "Fight" goes straight to the vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After /k/, /ɡ/, /p/, /b/ or /f/, the /r/ pulls the lips and tongue back, while /l/ keeps the tongue tip forward.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips slightly rounded through the cluster for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start and end. Dull or bright vowel?
quests.explanation: The word was "truck", a short, dull vowel. "Track" opens the jaw wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front, open vowel made with the jaw low and lips slightly spread; /ʌ/ is a central, relaxed vowel that needs far less mouth opening.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth a little sideways. For /ʌ/ keep the mouth relaxed and only slightly open, with the tongue resting in the middle.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does a lip burst come before the /r/?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "ridge" started with the curled /r/. "Bridge" opens with a lip pop first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word has an extra /r/ right after the first consonant. That /r/ makes the beginning of the word sound curled and slightly longer, and the first stop loses some of its crispness.
quests.mouthPosition: After the first consonant, curl the tongue tip back for /r/ before the vowel. Without it, the consonant moves straight into the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel long and smiling, or short and half open?
quests.explanation: It was "beach": a long, high vowel before the /tʃ/. "Bench" is shorter, with a half-open vowel and a nasal hum before the hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One vowel is held with a smile (/iː/), the other is a short, half-open one (/e/).
quests.mouthPosition: The tongue is higher and tenser for /iː/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a curled /r/ after the /d/?
quests.explanation: Here, "dive" went directly from /d/ into the vowel. "Drive" curls the tongue for an /r/ before it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word has an extra /r/ right after the first consonant. That /r/ makes the beginning of the word sound curled and slightly longer, and the first stop loses some of its crispness.
quests.mouthPosition: After the first consonant, curl the tongue tip back for /r/ before the vowel. Without it, the consonant moves straight into the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Which vowel is rounded and deep?
quests.explanation: You heard "step": a crisp, half-open vowel. "Stop" is deeper and rounder.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a front vowel with spread lips and a half-open jaw; /ɒ/ is a back vowel with rounded lips and a more open jaw. Front and unrounded against back and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ keep the tongue forward and the lips relaxed or slightly spread. For /ɒ/ pull the tongue back, drop the jaw and round the lips a little.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: How does the last consonant start?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "watch" ended with a stop and then a hush. "Wash" is a smooth hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ = /t/ + /ʃ/ in one movement; /ʃ/ has no stop.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue seal against the ridge before release for /tʃ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Sharp hiss, or a soft stop at the end?
quests.explanation: That was "slice": the word ended with a hiss. "Slide" ends with a tongue-tip stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Stops end abruptly and fricatives can be prolonged.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the air flow continuously for the fricative.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you hold it for me?
quests.hint: Friction from the lip, or just breath?
quests.explanation: This time, "hold" began with breath only. "Fold" begins with a lip-and-teeth hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /f/ is a hiss made between the lower lip and the upper teeth; /h/ is a plain breath from the throat with no friction in the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /f/ bring the lower lip to the upper teeth and blow. For /h/ leave the lips apart and just breathe out.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips or back of the tongue for the first burst?
quests.explanation: The word was "blue": the lips popped open. "Glue" bursts from the back of the tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The bilabial stop closes at the lips; the velar stop closes at the back of the tongue. The bilabial release sounds lower and fuller; the velar sounds deeper and hollow.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the lips for the bilabial; lift the back of the tongue to the soft palate for the velar.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Which burst comes from the back of the tongue?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "crush" began with a back-of-the-tongue burst and a breathy release. "Brush" begins with a lip burst.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lips versus tongue back, same voicing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel where the closure happens: lips or throat.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel, same ending. Touch or curl?
quests.explanation: It was "wrong": the tongue tip curled back and stayed away from the ridge. "Long" taps it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contact versus no contact: /l/ touches the ridge; /r/ hovers below it.
quests.mouthPosition: If your tongue touches the roof, you are making /l/; if it doesn't, /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Glide or burst at the start?
quests.explanation: Here, "rest" started with a smooth curled glide. "Test" starts with a short burst.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /t/ is a stop with a burst and a puff of air; /r/ is a smooth voiced glide with the tongue tip curled back and no closure.
quests.mouthPosition: For /t/ press the tongue tip against the ridge and release with a puff. For /r/ curl the tongue back without touching and let voiced air glide out.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Steady rounded vowel, or one that glides?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "fall": a steady rounded vowel with no glide. "Fail" ends with the mouth spreading.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ is a gliding vowel that ends spread and high; /ɔː/ is a steady, long, rounded vowel with no glide.
quests.mouthPosition: For /eɪ/ start half open and close toward a spread /ɪ/. For /ɔː/ round the lips from the start and hold the shape.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel tight or half open?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "spilling" used a tight, thin vowel. "Spelling" has a more open one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The vowels are close, so listen for jaw opening: /ɪ/ feels tight and closed, /e/ feels a little more open.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɪ/ with hardly any jaw movement, then drop the jaw a little for /e/.
